title: Centred etale coordinate differences along the diagonal
statement: Let h:U→V be a scheme morphism with a separated etale coordinate map [def-weil-etale-morphism] u:U→A^d_V [def-sbc-affine-space] over V, including d=0. Define the difference map U×_V U→A^d_U over the first projection by the coordinate functions y_i−x_i. There is an open neighbourhood O of the diagonal and a section s:U→O whose composite with the inclusion is the diagonal, such that the difference map restricted to O is etale and its square with s, the identity of U and the standard zero section is Cartesian. The statement includes empty U.

source.place: Step 1: etale coordinate differences and the centred Cartesian zero-section neighbourhood

proof.text: Base-change u to obtain the raw second-coordinate map over U. Translation by minus the first coordinates is an affine-space automorphism. Its composite with the raw map is the difference map, so that map is etale. Cache this calculation before the cone argument.

The centred etale chart geometry gives an open neighbourhood O, a section lifting the diagonal, and a pullback square over the affine-space diagonal. The difference coordinates vanish on the section. For a cone over the difference map and zero section, the structure-map equation identifies its base map, and coordinatewise y_i−x_i=0 supplies the original affine-diagonal cone equation. Its universal lift therefore satisfies both required cone equations and is unique. The same argument handles zero coordinates and the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem chartCoordinateDifferences_neighbourhood {U V : Scheme.{u}}
    (d : ℕ) (h : U ⟶ V) (u : U ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V)
    [Etale u] [IsSeparated u]
    (w : u ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) V ↘ V) = h) :
    ∃ (O : (pullback h h).Opens) (s : U ⟶ O.toScheme),
      s ≫ O.ι = pullback.diagonal h ∧
      Etale (O.ι ≫ chartCoordinateDifferences d h u) ∧
      IsPullback s (𝟙 U) (O.ι ≫ chartCoordinateDifferences d h u)
        (AffineSpace.zeroSection (ULift.{u} (Fin d)) U)
